title: bug: STREAM_JSON_PARSER (and its ps1 twin) appends a tool path containing a line break, forging a second TOOL witness line
description: scripts/moe-agent.sh STREAM_JSON_PARSER harvest() writes to_top_rel(raw) + '\n' with no control-character check, so an Edit/Write file_path or Serena create_text_file relative_path like 'a.py\nsrc/other.ts' (a legal Linux filename) appends 'src/other.ts' as its own TOOL witness. task-4b0609d1's codex helper (scripts/prompt-cache-witness.mjs toTopRel) refuses any [\u0000-\u001f] path with the WARN, row N15; port that refusal to the sh parser and check the ps1 Get-MoeToolWrittenPaths twin.
definitionOfDone: sh STREAM_JSON_PARSER and the ps1 twin refuse a harvested path containing a control character (WARN, no line), proven by a launcher test row each

implementationPlan.description:
sh fix plus its test row (scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs).

The fix goes in STREAM_JSON_PARSER's to_top_rel (moe-agent.sh ~8318), copying the refusal in prompt-cache-witness.mjs toTopRel (line ~70). Refuse the FINAL remainder p when `re.search(r'[\x00-\x1f]', p)` matches:
- in the absolute branch, right after the top prefix is sliced off (check `p[len(top) + 1:]`, then return it);
- in the relative branch, beside the existing '..' check, before `rel + p`.
Return None in both cases. harvest() already turns None into its `  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: <raw>` line and writes nothing, so the forged second line can no longer reach MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE.
- Keep raw.strip() as it is: a trailing newline that strip() removes stays accepted, exactly as the codex helper's trim does.
- Add one comment line above the check: a control character (a line break) would append a second, forged witness line, and prompt-cache-witness.mjs refuses the same set.
- Change nothing else in the parser. Peer row 7db14e2d edits only its header comment, a separate hunk.
- Editing rule for moe-agent.sh (a running seat hot-reloads it): write the whole edited file to a temp file on the same filesystem, run `bash -n` on it, then one `mv -f` over the original. Never edit in place.

Test: one new `test(...)` in importee-guard-bash.test.mjs, mirroring prompt-cache-witness.test.mjs N15. Spawn the extracted `streamParser` exactly as the fixture helper does (python -c, events piped as JSON lines), with env MOE_GIT_TOP=root, MOE_GIT_REL='', MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT=root and MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE=<scratch>/tools. Feed successful results (is_error false) for:
- (a) an Edit with file_path 'ok.txt\nforged.txt';
- (b) a Write with file_path `${root}/a.txt\rforged.txt` (absolute);
- (c) mcp__serena__create_text_file with relative_path 'b.py\nforged.py';
- (d) a control: an Edit with file_path 'plain.txt'.
Assert exit 0, and that the tools file's lines deep-equal ['plain.txt'], which proves the row is not vacuous. Assert stdout includes `WARN + raw + '\n'` for each of a-c, where raw is the joined Serena path for (c), exactly as harvest prints it.
Error handling: a malformed path must never raise inside the stream loop. to_top_rel only returns None, so harvest's existing per-path continue holds.
implementationPlan.note: to_top_rel refuses [\x00-\x1f] in both branches (edited in place with Edit per governor ruling); bash -n OK; new test passes.

implementationPlan.description:
ps1 twin plus its test row (scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/importee-guard.ps1).

The fix goes in Get-MoeToolWrittenPaths (moe-agent.ps1 ~5426). In the per-path loop, after `$tp` is computed:
- treat `$tp -match '[\x00-\x1f]'` exactly like an empty $tp: print the existing `  [attribution] tool path outside the repo dropped: $p` line and `continue`, so nothing reaches $script:MoeToolWritten or the daemon's touchedPaths;
- add the same one-line comment as the sh twin.
Keep moe-agent.ps1's UTF-8 BOM and LF endings. Stay PS 5.1 compatible. Check that `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` reports no errors before saving.

Test: in importee-guard.ps1, after the existing stream-parser rows and before the summary line:
- reset $script:MoeToolWritten, MoeToolPending and MoeToolSettled as the earlier rows do;
- set `$serenaProject = $fixtureRoot`, because the Serena branch joins against it.
Send through Send-ReviewToolUse / Send-ReviewToolResult with $false:
- (a) Edit with file_path "ok.txt`nforged.txt";
- (b) Write with file_path (Join-Path $fixtureRoot "a.txt`rforged.txt");
- (c) mcp__serena__create_text_file with relative_path "b.py`nforged.py".
Capture the Write-Host output with `6>&1` and assert it contains the dropped line for each. Then `Assert-ReviewWitnessCount 'control-character-path-refused' 0`. Then send (d) a Write of (Join-Path $fixtureRoot 'plain.txt') and assert the count is 1, so the row is not vacuous.
Error handling: the check runs on a string and cannot throw; the stream loop's existing try/catch is untouched.
implementationPlan.note: Get-MoeToolWrittenPaths drops a $tp with [\x00-\x1f] via the existing dropped line. New importee-guard.ps1 rows: 3 dropped-line, count 0, plain count 1. Test var renamed $ctrl because $case collides with the script's -Case param. BOM kept, no CR.

implementationPlan.description:
Final adversarial self-review, once, over this task's diff. Load adversarial-self-review and check:
1. Can a control character still reach a witness line? Try:
   - '\t' and '\x1f' inside the path;
   - a path that is only control characters after strip;
   - an absolute path whose control character sits right after the top prefix;
   - a Serena summary path from replace_in_files (serena_changed output flows through the same to_top_rel).
2. Is any LEGIT path now refused? Non-ASCII Unicode, spaces and '#' must still be witnessed. Only U+0000-U+001F is refused, exactly the codex helper's set, not DEL or C1.
3. The twins refuse on the same remainder (the post-top TOP-relative path) and keep their existing message texts. parity-check passes.
4. Hot-reload safety: moe-agent.sh was saved by an atomic mv after bash -n, and the ps1 keeps its BOM and LF.
5. Scope: no other behaviour changed. In particular, the absolute-path '..'/blank tightening the codex helper also has is NOT ported. That is out of this DoD; note it in the summary rather than fixing it.
If any byte changes, re-run step 3's command and submit that last output.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- (1) Sanitize: replace or strip the control characters. Rejected: it would witness a path git never has, and it diverges from the codex helper's whole-path refusal (N15).
- (2) Check the raw input before strip(). Rejected: a trailing newline is stripped harmlessly today, and the codex helper trims before checking too. Checking the final remainder matches it exactly.
- (3) Also port the helper's absolute '..'/blank tightening. Rejected as out of scope. The DoD names only control characters, so it is noted for follow-up.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The sh harvest goes through STREAM_JSON_PARSER: harvest() calls to_top_rel(raw), which returns None, then the WARN line `  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: %s`. Otherwise it appends `r + '\n'` to MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE. That newline-delimited file is why an embedded '\n' forges a second witness.
- The ps1 twin keeps the paths in the $script:MoeToolWritten hashtable, through Register-MoeToolWrite / Complete-MoeToolWrite. They then feed Resolve-MoeAttribution and record_commit touchedPaths. There is no file, but the refusal keeps the twins in parity and keeps junk paths out of the ledger.
- Tests:
  - importee-guard-bash.test.mjs extracts the parser text from moe-agent.sh and spawns it with python;
  - importee-guard.ps1 loads the functions through the AST and has the Send-ReviewToolUse / Send-ReviewToolResult / Assert-ReviewWitnessCount helpers. It runs in CI under both powershell and pwsh.
- Ordering: peer 7db14e2d edits only STREAM_JSON_PARSER's header comment. It is already upstream of this row through the WT chain (WT-06 depends on it).
planningNotes.risks:
- moe-agent.sh is hot-reloaded by running seats. Use the atomic save rule (`mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse`).
- The ps1 Serena branch reads $serenaProject from script scope, and the test must set it.
- Write-Host goes to stream 6 in PS 5.1: capture it with 6>&1.
